newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends slightly up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends slightly up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly up on Thursday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 20,430 yuan ($2,461) per tonne, rising 30 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,400 and hit a high of 20,580.
December rose 100 to 20,000, January 70 to 20,210, February 90 to 20,430, April 80 to 20,480, May 120 to 20,520 and the first traded June contract ended at 20,550.
Combined volume fell to 72,310 tonnes from 78,250.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session.
Traders said LME gains kept Shanghai copper steady and liquidation dominated today's trading.
"Long and short position holders liquidated their positions for profits and stayed on the sidelines after sharp rises over the past few days," one trader said.
"Long position holders have not lost their confidence because of good technical charts but need a break after sharp gains," a second trader said.
Traders expect copper to move around the 20,500-yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up. December rose 140 to 13,620 yuan per tonne, January 200 to 13,750.
Combined volume rose to 1,850 tonnes from 340.
